claim: Democrats secured majority control of the House.
evidence: ABC News live blog, Nov. 4, 2026, 4:10 PM EST (the source listed as no. 3 in the draft): projecting Democrats take the House. Washington Examiner 2026 midterm live blog, updated Nov. 5, 2026, 9:12 AM (not in the draft's source list): 240 House seats, 48 races still open.
note: Supported as a projection. The draft's own caution (not certified) is correct; 'secured' in the dek should read 'are projected to have won'.

claim: Democrats secured majority control of the Senate; the seat count is in flux.
evidence: ABC News live blog, Nov. 4, 2026, 4:10 PM EST (the source listed as no. 3 in the draft): projecting Democrats take the Senate. Washington Examiner 2026 midterm live blog, updated Nov. 5, 2026, 9:12 AM (not in the draft's source list): 54 Senate seats, Alaska and Mississippi uncalled.
note: Supported as a projection. The Examiner count (54) is more specific than the draft, which is consistent with 'in flux'.

claim: President Donald Trump remains in office, so government is divided.
evidence: Public record: a Republican president serves through January 2029.
note: No source needed beyond the public record.

claim: The result was a reversal larger than many election observers expected.
evidence: Pre-election forecasts found (Sabato's Crystal Ball: Democrats +6 Senate, +24 House) do not show the outcome relative to expectations.
note: An editorial comparison with no cited source. Needs a named forecast and the actual gain, or removal.

claim: Voters expressed dissatisfaction with the cost of living, the direction of the country and the conduct of the presidency.
evidence: AP-NORC (pre-election) shows the economy and the cost of living as the top priorities. The AP Voter Poll page (source 5) could not be opened.
note: Cost of living supported by pre-election polling only. 'Conduct of the presidency' needs the AP Voter Poll.

evidence: ABC News live blog, Nov. 4, 2026, 4:10 PM EST (the source listed as no. 3 in the draft): letter to colleagues, 'I write to humbly request your support in connection with my candidacy.'

evidence: ABC News live blog, Nov. 4, 2026, 4:10 PM EST (the source listed as no. 3 in the draft): House Democrats hold leadership elections on Nov. 18; Jeffries needs 218 floor votes in January.
note: Supported for House Democrats. The Senate Democratic date is not in any readable source.

evidence: Washington Examiner 2026 midterm live blog, updated Nov. 5, 2026, 9:12 AM (not in the draft's source list): Kansas (Hamilton over Marshall), Texas (Talarico over Paxton), Iowa (Turek, past 50 seats) and South Carolina (Andrews) are reported; Ohio is not supported for the Senate (Acton over Ramaswamy is the governor's race).
note: Ohio Senate is unverified and may be wrong. Texas, Iowa and South Carolina were not shown as flips in the one readable source. The Reuters takeaways (source 4) could not be opened.

evidence: No margin data was found. The 2024 presidential results are public but were not compared here.
